subproblems.title: Upper Density Theorem for μHE[n] off a Borel set of finite measure (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set with Hⁿ(S) < ∞, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure). Then for Hⁿ-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P: if x ∉ S, then Hⁿ(S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ)) / ρⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. The quotient is taken in [0, ∞] with ρⁿ := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet S → μHE[n] S ≠ ∞ → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), x ∉ S → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => μHE[n] (S ∩ closedBall x ρ) / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3, Lemma 3.4 (5-times covering lemma) and the proof of the Upper Density Theorem 3.6 (book/chapter-01.txt lines 602–721), with Theorem 1.15(2) (inner approximation by closed sets). This is the Upper Density Theorem invoked in Step 2 of the parent proof, for one Borel set of finite measure. The localization to U is the sibling local_density_zero.

Notation.
- μ := μHE[n].
- μH := μH[(n : ℝ)] is Mathlib's Hausdorff measure: μH(E) = sup over δ > 0 of inf Σ_i (diam C_i)ⁿ, over countable covers of E by sets C_i with diam C_i ≤ δ.
- Mathlib defines μ = c • μH with the finite constant c := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ [0, ∞) (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). So μ(E) = c·μH(E) for every set E, and μH(E) = 0 implies μ(E) = 0.
- For ρ > 0 put ρⁿ := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ ∈ (0, ∞). For x ∈ ℝ^P put q_x(ρ) := μ(S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ ∈ [0, ∞].

Departures from the printed text.
(a) SimonGMT's formal 3.6 (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6, Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean) is outside the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission: #check reports an unknown identifier. The printed argument is therefore reproduced with Mathlib.
(b) The proof of 3.6 uses 3.3 only to produce a null set. So in Simon's proof of 3.3 every selected ball is enlarged: this is the case N = 0 of the printed covering A₁ ⊆ ⋃_{j≤N} B_j ∪ ⋃_{j>N} B̂_j. This avoids Corollary 3.5 and gives the constant 6ⁿ instead of 1. Since only the centres need to be covered, radius 3ρ' replaces 5ρ'.
(c) Lemma 3.4(*) is used in Mathlib's form Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement, with factor τ = 2.
(d) Balls are closed, as in Simon (3.1), and the density is normalized by ρⁿ instead of ω_n ρⁿ. This does not affect vanishing.
(e) The disjoint subfamily is countable because ℝ^P is separable (Simon's remark in the proof of 3.4(i), chapter-01.txt lines 631–633).
(f) The condition "q_x(ρ) > t for arbitrarily small ρ > 0" plays the role of Simon's Θ^{*n} > γ.

1. (Reduction to threshold sets.)
- Fix x ∉ S. Since q_x ≥ 0, q_x(ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 if and only if, for every ε > 0, q_x(ρ) ≤ ε for all sufficiently small ρ > 0 (Mathlib ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero).
- So if q_x(ρ) does not tend to 0, there is ε > 0 with q_x(ρ) > ε for arbitrarily small ρ > 0, i.e. frequently in 𝓝[>]0.
- Choose k ∈ ℕ with (k : [0,∞])⁻¹ < ε (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt). Then t_k := (k+1)⁻¹ ≤ k⁻¹ < ε, so x belongs to N_k := {x ∈ ℝ^P : x ∉ S and q_x(ρ) > t_k for arbitrarily small ρ > 0}. Here t_k ∈ (0, ∞).
- Hence every x at which "x ∉ S ⟹ q_x(ρ) → 0" fails lies in ⋃_{k∈ℕ} N_k.
- By countable subadditivity it suffices to prove μ(N_k) = 0 for every k. No measurability of N_k is needed: an a.e. statement only requires its failure set to lie in a null set (ae_iff, measure_mono_null, measure_iUnion_null).

2. (Comparison lemma: Simon 3.3 with a crude constant.)
Claim. Let t ∈ (0, ∞), E ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary and G ⊆ ℝ^P Borel. Suppose that for every x ∈ E and every δ > 0 there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with t·ρⁿ ≤ μ(G ∩ closedBall(x, ρ)). Then t·μH(E) ≤ 6ⁿ·μ(G).
Proof of the claim.
- Fix j ∈ ℕ and δ_j := 1/(j+1). Let T_j be the set of pairs (c, ρ) ∈ ℝ^P × ℝ with c ∈ E, 0 < ρ < δ_j and t·ρⁿ ≤ μ(G ∩ closedBall(c, ρ)). Write B(c, ρ) := closedBall(c, ρ); it is a nonempty closed ball of radius ≤ δ_j.
- By the Vitali covering lemma (Simon 3.4; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement with radius function (c, ρ) ↦ ρ, τ = 2 and radius bound δ_j) there is u_j ⊆ T_j with two properties. The balls B(a), a ∈ u_j, are pairwise disjoint. For every (c, ρ) ∈ T_j there is (c', ρ') ∈ u_j with B(c, ρ) ∩ B(c', ρ') ≠ ∅ and ρ ≤ 2ρ'.
 (i) u_j is countable. Its balls are pairwise disjoint, each has nonempty interior (it contains ball(c', ρ') with ρ' > 0), and ℝ^P is separable (Mathlib Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior).
 (ii) E ⊆ ⋃_{(c',ρ')∈u_j} closedBall(c', 3ρ'). For x ∈ E, the hypothesis with δ = δ_j gives ρ with (x, ρ) ∈ T_j. Pick (c', ρ') ∈ u_j and w ∈ B(x, ρ) ∩ B(c', ρ') with ρ ≤ 2ρ'. Then dist(x, c') ≤ dist(x, w) + dist(w, c') ≤ ρ + ρ' ≤ 3ρ'.
 (iii) t·Σ_{(c',ρ')∈u_j} ρ'ⁿ ≤ Σ_{u_j} μ(G ∩ B(c', ρ')) = μ(⋃_{u_j} G ∩ B(c', ρ')) ≤ μ(G). The first inequality is the defining inequality of T_j ⊇ u_j. The equality is countable additivity of μ on the pairwise disjoint Borel sets G ∩ B(c', ρ') (Mathlib measure_biUnion).
 (iv) ediam closedBall(c', 3ρ') ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(6ρ') ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(6δ_j), by the triangle inequality. Hence (ediam closedBall(c', 3ρ'))ⁿ ≤ 6ⁿ·ρ'ⁿ, and by (iii) Σ_{u_j} (ediam closedBall(c', 3ρ'))ⁿ ≤ 6ⁿ·Σ_{u_j} ρ'ⁿ ≤ 6ⁿ·μ(G)/t.
- For each j, the countable family {closedBall(c', 3ρ') : (c', ρ') ∈ u_j} covers E by (ii), with diameters ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(6δ_j) → 0.
- Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum, with the countable index type u_j at stage j, gives μH(E) ≤ liminf_j Σ_{u_j} (ediam closedBall(c', 3ρ'))ⁿ. By (iv) this is ≤ 6ⁿ·μ(G)/t.
- Multiplying by t ∈ (0, ∞) gives t·μH(E) ≤ 6ⁿ·μ(G), which proves the claim.

3. (Simon's proof of 3.6: each N_k is null.)
- Fix k, put t := t_k, and let ε be a positive real number.
- The measure μ⌞S is finite, because μ(S) < ∞, and it is a Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P. Hence it is weakly regular (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure).
- Since S is Borel, Simon 1.15(2) (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_diff_lt for μ⌞S) gives a closed set F ⊆ S with μ(S ∖ F) = (μ⌞S)(S ∖ F) < t·ε/6ⁿ. This bound is a positive real number. Put G := S ∖ F, a Borel set.
- We verify the hypothesis of Step 2 for E := N_k and this G. Let x ∈ N_k and δ > 0.
  - Since x ∉ S ⊇ F and F is closed, there is r₁ > 0 with ball(x, r₁) ∩ F = ∅.
  - q_x(ρ) > t for arbitrarily small ρ > 0, and (0, min(δ, r₁/2)) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>]0. So there is ρ ∈ (0, min(δ, r₁/2)) with q_x(ρ) > t. Since ρⁿ ∈ (0, ∞), this means μ(S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ)) > t·ρⁿ.
  - closedBall(x, ρ) ⊆ ball(x, r₁) does not meet F, so S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ) = G ∩ closedBall(x, ρ).
  - Hence t·ρⁿ ≤ μ(G ∩ closedBall(x, ρ)) with 0 < ρ < δ.
- Step 2 now gives t·μH(N_k) ≤ 6ⁿ·μ(G) < 6ⁿ·(t·ε/6ⁿ) = t·ε, because 6ⁿ ∈ (0, ∞). Since t ∈ (0, ∞), μH(N_k) < ε.
- As ε > 0 was arbitrary, μH(N_k) = 0, and therefore μ(N_k) = c·μH(N_k) = 0.

4. (Conclusion.) By Step 3 and countable subadditivity, μ(⋃_k N_k) = 0. By Step 1, every x at which "x ∉ S ⟹ q_x(ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0" fails lies in ⋃_k N_k. Hence for μ-almost every x: if x ∉ S, then μ(S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. This is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: If x ∉ S and q_x(ρ) = μHE[n](S ∩ closedBall(x,ρ))/ρⁿ does not tend to 0, then x lies in a threshold set N_k = {x ∉ S : q_x(ρ) > 1/(k+1) for arbitrarily small ρ}. It suffices that each N_k is μHE[n]-null.

Comparison lemma (Simon 3.3 with N = 0 and a crude constant): Vitali selection with factor 2, countability by separability, additivity of μHE[n] on the disjoint balls and the Hausdorff covering bound give t·μH[n](E) ≤ 6ⁿ·μHE[n](G).

Simon's proof of 3.6: take a closed F ⊆ S with μHE[n](S∖F) small (weak regularity of the finite measure μHE[n]⌞S). Near x ∉ F, S and G = S∖F agree in small balls, so t·μH[n](N_k) ≤ 6ⁿ·μHE[n](S∖F) is arbitrarily small.
Hence μH[n](N_k) = 0, so μHE[n](N_k) = 0, and the implication x ∉ S ⟹ q_x(ρ) → 0 holds μHE[n]-a.e.

subproblems.title: Upper Density Theorem off a set of locally finite measure in an open set (Simon Ch. 1, Remark 3.7(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with Hⁿ(S ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Then for Hⁿ-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P: if x ∈ U and x ∉ S, then Hⁿ(S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. The quotient is taken in [0, ∞] with ρⁿ := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U S : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet S → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (S ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), x ∈ U → x ∉ S → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => μHE[n] (S ∩ closedBall x ρ) / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Remark 3.7(2) (book/chapter-01.txt lines 705–711) and Steps 1–3 of the parent proof. Cover U by countably many open sets whose closures are compact subsets of U, apply the Upper Density Theorem (sibling upper_density_zero) to the part of S in each, and localize. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; for ρ > 0, ρⁿ := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ ∈ (0, ∞).

1. (Countable cover of U.)
- For each y ∈ U choose ε_y > 0 with ball(y, ε_y) ⊆ U (U is open) and put r_y := ε_y/2. Then closedBall(y, r_y) ⊆ ball(y, ε_y) ⊆ U.
- The open balls ball(y, r_y), y ∈ U, cover U and are contained in U.
- Since ℝ^P is second countable, a countable subfamily has the same union (Lindelöf; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable). So there is a countable set D ⊆ U with U = ⋃_{y∈D} ball(y, r_y).
- This plays the role of the parent's exhaustion U = ⋃_m V_m; any countable cover of U by open sets with compact closures in U works the same way.

2. (Finite-measure pieces.)
- For y ∈ D put S_y := S ∩ ball(y, r_y), a Borel set.
- closedBall(y, r_y) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and contained in U, so μ(S_y) ≤ μ(S ∩ closedBall(y, r_y)) < ∞ by the hypothesis.
- By the sibling theorem upper_density_zero applied to S_y: for μ-a.e. x, if x ∉ S_y then μ(S_y ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.

3. (Countably many a.e. statements.) D is countable, so for μ-a.e. x the conclusion of Step 2 holds simultaneously for every y ∈ D (Mathlib MeasureTheory.ae_ball_iff: a countable intersection of conull sets is conull).

4. (Localization.) Let x be such a point with x ∈ U and x ∉ S.
- By Step 1 choose y ∈ D with x ∈ ball(y, r_y). Since S_y ⊆ S, x ∉ S_y, so by Step 3 μ(S_y ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
- ball(y, r_y) is open and contains x, so there is s > 0 with ball(x, s) ⊆ ball(y, r_y).
- For 0 < ρ < s, closedBall(x, ρ) ⊆ ball(x, s) ⊆ ball(y, r_y), hence S_y ∩ closedBall(x, ρ) = S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ).
- The two quotient functions therefore agree on (0, s), which belongs to 𝓝[>]0. Eventually equal functions have the same limit (Filter.Tendsto.congr'), so μ(S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.

5. (Conclusion.) By Steps 3 and 4, for μ-almost every x: if x ∈ U and x ∉ S, then μ(S ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. This is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover U by countably many open balls ball(y, r_y), y ∈ D, whose closures closedBall(y, r_y) are compact subsets of U (Lindelöf).

Each piece S ∩ ball(y, r_y) is Borel with finite μHE[n]-measure. The Upper Density Theorem (sibling upper_density_zero) gives vanishing density of the piece at a.e. point outside it, simultaneously for the countably many y.
For x ∈ U ∖ S pick y with x ∈ ball(y, r_y). For small ρ, S and the piece agree inside closedBall(x, ρ), so the density quotient of S at x tends to 0.

subproblems.title: Hⁿ-measure of a blow-up inside a ball (translation invariance and scaling)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, r, R ∈ ℝ with r > 0, and S ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set. Let η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) be SimonGMT's blowUpMap x r, and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Then, in [0, ∞], Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S) ∩ closedBall(0, R)) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ · Hⁿ(S ∩ closedBall(x, r·R)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (r R : ℝ) (S : Set (Euclid P)), 0 < r → μHE[n] (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' S ∩ closedBall 0 R) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ ^ n * μHE[n] (S ∩ closedBall x (r * R))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4(b) of the parent proof: "Hⁿ is translation invariant and Hⁿ(λ⁻¹S) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(S); so η(B) ∩ B_R(0) = η(B ∩ B_{λR}(x)) has measure λ^{−n}Hⁿ(B ∩ B_{λR}(x))". This is the scaling identity in Simon's proof of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (book/chapter-03.txt lines 126–134), here with closed balls. Notation: η := blowUpMap x r, so η(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x); μ := μHE[n]; r > 0 throughout.

1. (Set identity.) We show η(S) ∩ closedBall(0, R) = η(S ∩ closedBall(x, rR)).
- For every z, ‖η(z)‖ = |r⁻¹|·‖z − x‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖. Since r > 0, r⁻¹‖z − x‖ ≤ R ⟺ ‖z − x‖ ≤ rR.
- If y = η(z) with z ∈ S and ‖y‖ ≤ R, then ‖z − x‖ ≤ rR. So z ∈ S ∩ closedBall(x, rR) and y ∈ η(S ∩ closedBall(x, rR)).
- Conversely, if z ∈ S and ‖z − x‖ ≤ rR, then η(z) ∈ η(S) and ‖η(z)‖ ≤ R.
- For R < 0 both sides are empty, consistently with the computation.

2. (Decomposition of η.) Let τ(z) := z + (−x), a translation. Then η(z) = r⁻¹ • τ(z) for every z. Hence η(T) = r⁻¹ • τ(T) for every T ⊆ ℝ^P, where c • A := {c·a : a ∈ A}.

3. (Scaling of μ.)
- τ is an isometry, so μ(τ(T)) = μ(T) for every T ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- Since r⁻¹ ≠ 0, Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ gives μ(r⁻¹ • A) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ · μ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P.
- Since r > 0, ‖r⁻¹‖₊ is the nonnegative real r⁻¹. Its image in [0, ∞] is (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹, the inverse of the nonzero finite value ENNReal.ofReal r.
- Therefore μ(η(T)) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ · μ(T) for every T ⊆ ℝ^P.
- Equivalently, η = τ' ∘ h with h the homothety of centre x and ratio r⁻¹ and τ' the translation by −x; Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image gives the same factor.

4. (Conclusion.) Apply Step 3 to T := S ∩ closedBall(x, r·R) and use Step 1: μ(η(S) ∩ closedBall(0, R)) = μ(η(T)) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ · μ(S ∩ closedBall(x, r·R)). This is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: η_{x,r}(S) ∩ closedBall(0,R) = η_{x,r}(S ∩ closedBall(x, rR)), since ‖η_{x,r}(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ and r > 0.
η_{x,r}(T) = r⁻¹ • (T − x). Translations preserve μHE[n] (isometry), and μHE[n](r⁻¹ • A) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ μHE[n](A) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ μHE[n](A).
Combining both gives μHE[n](η_{x,r}(S) ∩ closedBall(0,R)) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ μHE[n](S ∩ closedBall(x, rR)).

subproblems.title: Same approximate tangent spaces where the difference has zero n-density (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 '⇒')
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let A ⊆ B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel sets, x ∈ ℝ^P and r₀ > 0 with Hⁿ(B ∩ closedBall(x, r₀)) < ∞, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Suppose Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0, with the quotient in [0, ∞] and ρⁿ := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ. Then for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, B has approximate tangent space Q at x if and only if A does. Here 'M has approximate tangent space Q at x' is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4): dim Q = n, and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A B : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (r₀ : ℝ), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → 0 < r₀ → μHE[n] (B ∩ closedBall x r₀) ≠ ∞ → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => μHE[n] ((B \ A) ∩ closedBall x ρ) / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 4–6 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (book/chapter-03.txt lines 113–143). There the integrals of f over η_{x,λ}(B) and η_{x,λ}(A) differ by the integral over η_{x,λ}(B ∖ A), which is bounded by sup|f|·λ^{−n}Hⁿ(B_{λR}(x) ∩ (B ∖ A)) → 0. Closed balls replace the parent's open balls; D ∩ B_s(x) ⊆ D ∩ closedBall(x, s), so nothing is lost.

Notation.
- μ := μHE[n].
- For r ≠ 0, η_r := blowUpMap x r, so η_r(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x).
- For ρ > 0, ρⁿ := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)ⁿ.
- For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and M ⊆ ℝ^P put I_M(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ, the Bochner integral with respect to μ restricted to η_r(M).
- By definition, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q means: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), I_M(r) → ∫_Q f dμ as r → 0 along 𝓝[>]0.

1. (Properties of η_r for r > 0.)
- η_r is injective: r⁻¹(z − x) = r⁻¹(w − x) implies z − x = w − x, so z = w.
- For every T ⊆ ℝ^P, η_r(T) = g_r⁻¹(T) with g_r(y) := x + r·y. If y = η_r(z) with z ∈ T, then g_r(y) = z ∈ T. Conversely, if g_r(y) ∈ T, then y = η_r(g_r(y)).
- g_r is continuous, so η_r(T) is Borel whenever T is Borel.

2. (Fix f.) Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
- f is continuous with compact support, so it is bounded: |f(y)| ≤ C for all y, for some real C (Mathlib Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
- Its topological support is compact, hence bounded, so it lies in closedBall(0, R₁) for some R₁. Put R := max(R₁, 1) > 0.
- Then f(y) = 0 for every y ∉ closedBall(0, R).

3. (Finiteness and integrability for small r.)
- Let 0 < r < r₀/R, so that rR < r₀. The interval (0, r₀/R) belongs to 𝓝[>]0.
- For T ⊆ B, the sibling blowup_measure_scaling gives μ(η_r(T) ∩ closedBall(0, R)) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ · μ(T ∩ closedBall(x, rR)) ≤ (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ · μ(B ∩ closedBall(x, r₀)) < ∞. This uses T ∩ closedBall(x, rR) ⊆ B ∩ closedBall(x, r₀), the finiteness of (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ (as r > 0), and the hypothesis.
- Now let T ⊆ B be Borel. f is measurable and bounded by C on η_r(T) ∩ closedBall(0, R), a set of finite measure, so it is integrable there (Mathlib Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).
- f vanishes on η_r(T) ∖ closedBall(0, R), and η_r(T) is Borel by Step 1. So f is integrable on η_r(T) (Mathlib IntegrableOn.of_forall_diff_eq_zero).

4. (Splitting; parent Step 4(a),(c).) Let r be as in Step 3.
- Since A ⊆ B, η_r(B) = η_r(A) ∪ η_r(B ∖ A).
- The two images are disjoint, because η_r is injective and A ∩ (B ∖ A) = ∅.
- η_r(B ∖ A) is Borel, and f is integrable on η_r(A) and on η_r(B ∖ A) (Step 3 with T = A and T = B ∖ A).
- Additivity of the set integral over disjoint sets (Mathlib setIntegral_union) gives I_B(r) = I_A(r) + I_{B∖A}(r), i.e. I_B(r) − I_A(r) = I_{B∖A}(r).

5. (Estimate; parent Step 5.) Let r be as in Step 3 and K := closedBall(0, R).
- f = 0 on η_r(B ∖ A) ∖ K, so I_{B∖A}(r) = ∫_{η_r(B∖A) ∩ K} f dμ (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero).
- This set has finite measure by Step 3, and |f| ≤ C on it. Hence |I_{B∖A}(r)| ≤ C·m(r), where m(r) := μ(η_r(B ∖ A) ∩ K) viewed as a real number (Mathlib norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const).
- With ρ := rR > 0, blowup_measure_scaling gives μ(η_r(B ∖ A) ∩ K) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ · μ((B ∖ A) ∩ closedBall(x, rR)) = ENNReal.ofReal(R)ⁿ · [μ((B ∖ A) ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ].
- The second equality holds because ENNReal.ofReal(rR) = ENNReal.ofReal(r)·ENNReal.ofReal(R) (as r ≥ 0). So ρⁿ = ENNReal.ofReal(r)ⁿ·ENNReal.ofReal(R)ⁿ with both factors in (0, ∞), and ENNReal.ofReal(R)ⁿ·(1/ρⁿ) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ.
- These identities in [0, ∞] hold for every r > 0.

6. (Limit; end of parent Step 5.)
- The map r ↦ rR is continuous, vanishes at 0, and is positive for r > 0 because R > 0. So it maps 𝓝[>]0 into 𝓝[>]0 (Mathlib tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within).
- By the density hypothesis, the bracket in Step 5 tends to 0 as r ↓ 0. Multiplication by the finite constant ENNReal.ofReal(R)ⁿ keeps the limit 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul).
- So μ(η_r(B ∖ A) ∩ K) → 0 in [0, ∞] as r ↓ 0. Hence m(r) → 0 (ENNReal.toReal is continuous at 0), and C·m(r) → 0.
- By Steps 4–5, |I_B(r) − I_A(r)| ≤ C·m(r) for every r ∈ (0, r₀/R), a set in 𝓝[>]0. The squeeze theorem (Mathlib squeeze_zero_norm') gives I_B(r) − I_A(r) → 0 as r ↓ 0.

7. (Conclusion; parent Step 6.) Let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P. The condition finrank Q = n is the same on both sides.
- If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, then for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), I_A(r) = I_B(r) − (I_B(r) − I_A(r)) → ∫_Q f dμ − 0 = ∫_Q f dμ. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q.
- Conversely, if HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q, then I_B(r) = I_A(r) + (I_B(r) − I_A(r)) → ∫_Q f dμ + 0. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.
- This is the asserted equivalence for every Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: η_r = blowUpMap x r is injective and maps Borel sets to Borel sets. A test function f is bounded by C and vanishes off closedBall(0,R) with R > 0.

For 0 < r < r₀/R, the scaling identity (sibling blowup_measure_scaling) bounds μHE[n](η_r(B) ∩ closedBall(0,R)) by (ofReal r)⁻¹ⁿ μHE[n](B ∩ closedBall(x,r₀)) < ∞. So f is integrable on η_r(A) and η_r(B∖A), and ∫_{η_r(B)} f − ∫_{η_r(A)} f = ∫_{η_r(B∖A)} f.
|∫_{η_r(B∖A)} f| ≤ C·μHE[n](η_r(B∖A) ∩ closedBall(0,R)) = C·ofReal(R)ⁿ·μHE[n]((B∖A) ∩ closedBall(x,rR))/ofReal(rR)ⁿ. This tends to 0 as r ↓ 0 by the density hypothesis, since rR ↓ 0.
Hence the blow-up integrals of B and of A have the same limits for every f ∈ C_c, and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q for every Q.
